facts.label: Entity and perimeter map
facts.text: The registrant is Primo Brands Corporation (cover, page:1 of each report). The notes name different entities for debt. Under the First Lien Credit Agreement, Primo Brands is the parent borrower, Triton Water Holdings, Inc. and Primo Water Holdings Inc. are borrowers, and Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. is term loan administrative agent and collateral agent (10-Q Q3 page:16). The three series of senior notes are co-issued by Primo Water Holdings Inc. and Triton Water Holdings, Inc., described as indirect, wholly owned subsidiaries (10-K page:158). The 3.875% Senior Notes are described as secured and "guaranteed by the Company and substantially all of the Company's wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries" (10-K page:160), and the 6.250% Senior Notes as guaranteed "by the Company and certain subsidiaries" (10-K page:159). Security is described in the 10-K MD&A: the term loans are secured by a first-priority lien on substantially all of the issuers' and guarantors' current and fixed assets (page:95), the two secured note series rank pari passu with the credit agreement liens (page:98) and the 6.250% Senior Notes are "senior unsecured obligations" (page:99). No separate co-issuer or guarantor financial statements were located in the pack (searches for guarantor summarized financial information found none), so the consolidated statements are the only perimeter available. Whether the consolidated figures equal the restricted group is an unresolved distinction and is logged as a gap.

facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and limitations
facts.text: 1. Debt table and ladder are stale for the term loan. The 10-K ladder shows 2028 at "3,535.2" and a total of "5,078.3" (page:155), and the term loans then matured March 31, 2028 (page:156). The Q3 10-Q says the refinancing facility "will mature in March 2031" and amortizes 1.00% per annum (page:16). The 10-K ladder therefore cannot be used as the current wall. The Q3 report prints no new ladder (search of the Q3 10-Q for "maturities" found none), so a current ladder is a downstream derivation from the 10-K senior note maturities and the Q3 term loan terms. 2. Finance leases, other debt and revolver balance are not itemized at September 30, 2026. The Q3 fair-value table totals "5,017.5" (page:30) while the release prints "Total debt, excluding unamortized debt costs and discounts" of "5,249.7" (Q3 release page:14). The difference is tied out in ## Calculations and is not described in the Q3 report. The Q3 10-Q does not state a revolver drawn balance; the 10-K table shows the revolver as "—" at December 31, 2025 (page:154) and the MD&A says the company had "access to $750.0 million of revolving loan commitments (without giving effect to $163.4 million of outstanding letters of credit)" (10-Q Q3 page:51). 3. No reported covenant ratio. The Revolving Credit Facility requires "a first lien net leverage ratio of less than or equal to 5.00 to 1.00" and "a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.00 to 1.00" (10-Q Q3 page:17), and the company states it "was in compliance with all covenants" (page:18). Neither the first lien net leverage nor the interest coverage ratio as computed under the credit agreement is printed. The release's net leverage ratio of 3.32x (Q3 release page:14) is a management measure on total debt less unrestricted cash over TTM Adjusted EBITDA and is not stated to be the covenant definition. 4. Executed documents not supplied. The 10-K exhibit index lists the credit agreement and indentures by incorporation (page:116 to page:118) and the pack contains none of their text. The springing maturity on the revolver is described only as "subject to a springing maturity based on conditions set forth in the Amended Credit Agreement" (10-Q Q3 page:17); the condition is not stated. 5. Management measures versus filings. Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow, adjusted free cash flow and net leverage are non-GAAP and appear in the releases and the 10-Q MD&A; the filed statements control GAAP facts. The TTM Adjusted EBITDA of 1,436.1 combines a FY2025 figure, which the 10-K also prints (page:86), with nine-month figures from the Q3 release. For nine months 2026 the bridge runs from EBITDA of "977.6" to Adjusted EBITDA of "1,102.0", and its largest item is acquisition, integration and restructuring expenses of "91.2" (Q3 release page:11). 6. Comparability. The releases restate the 2025 comparison base to exclude exited operations (Q3 release page:13), and the discontinued operations line in 2025 (net loss of "(32.6)" for nine months 2025, Q3 10-Q page:5) has no 2026 counterpart. Prior-period amounts "have been reclassified to conform with the 2026 presentation" (Q3 10-Q page:10) without a reclassification schedule in the text read. 7. Contingent claims without estimates. The securities class action, the consumer class action and the Patane spring-water labelling class action are disclosed in Note 14 (page:34 to page:38). The company states it is "unable to reasonably estimate the amount or range of possible loss, if any, in excess of the amounts accrued" (page:34). The Patane parties scheduled a second mediation for November 19, 2026 (page:38), after the cutoff, so any outcome is outside this pack. 8. Not supplied. Earnings presentations (the releases refer to a supplemental presentation on the company website, which is not in the pack), executed legal documents, market quotes, peers, valuation inputs, deal terms and a discrete Q4 2025 quarter. A Q4 2025 figure would be a downstream derivation from the 10-K and interim sources, not a source. 9. Extraction only. All seven files are text conversions; charts and images are not inspected, and successful extraction is not a fidelity review. Not every chunk was read line by line in this review; the chunks read are those cited.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Primo Brands Corporation reports as one registrant with one segment, so the base is a single consolidated set of statements rather than a segment mosaic. Through nine months 2026, net sales were 5,243.3, up 2.6% on 5,109.9, and Adjusted EBITDA was 1,102.0, down 1.0% from 1,112.7, because cost of sales grew faster than sales on freight and materials costs (Q3 10-Q page:49). Q3 2026 was better than the first half: net sales rose 3.1% to 1,821.0, Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.6% to 411.0 and the margin was 22.6% against 22.9% a year earlier. EBITDA before add-backs rose much faster than Adjusted EBITDA (396.9 against 313.1 in Q3) because lower integration costs (add-back of 23.7 against 88.2) and an unrealized gain of 26.1, both excluded from Adjusted EBITDA, flowed through, and the total add-backs shrank to 14.1 in Q3 2026 from 91.4 a year earlier. Trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 1,436.1 gives gross leverage of 3.66 times and net leverage of 3.32 times on the company's definition; on EBITDA before add-backs of 1,209.1 the ratios are 4.34 and 3.95 times. Cash paid for interest of 298.7 over the trailing twelve months is covered 4.81 times by Adjusted EBITDA. Operating cash flow was 625.3 for nine months against 477.2, with payables and accruals contributing 141.1 of the 148.1 improvement, partly offset by other working capital lines; a payables-driven gain can reverse. Liquidity of 1,063.8 is cash of 477.2 plus revolver commitments of 750.0 less 163.4 of letters of credit. The March 2026 refinancing moved the term loan to March 2031, so the nearest large maturities are the 3.875% notes in October 2028 and the 4.375% and 6.250% notes in April 2029. Four limits bind: Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure with large add-backs, covenant ratios are not printed, finance leases, other debt and the revolver balance are not itemized at September 30, 2026, and the maturity ladder after the refinancing is derived, not filed.

facts.label: Latest quarter and events to the cutoff
facts.text: - Financing. The Fifth Amendment of March 31, 2026 refinanced term loans of 3,067.6 into 3,090.0 maturing March 2031, a net principal increase of 22.4, with a loss on modification and extinguishment of debt of 17.7 in nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:16, page:17). No financing event on debt occurred in Q3 2026; term loan repayments were 7.8 (Q3 10-Q page:7). - Equity. On August 7, 2026 the sponsor affiliate Triton Water Equity Holdings sold 20,000,000 shares at 24.37 a share in a secondary offering, and the company bought back 410,340 shares from it for about 10.0 funded from cash; the company received no offering proceeds (Q3 10-Q page:19, page:61). - After quarter end. facts.label: Leverage
facts.text: Net debt fell to 4,772.5 at September 30, 2026 from 4,872.4 at December 31, 2025, a decrease of 99.9, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA fell to 1,436.1 from 1,446.8. Net leverage on the company's definition was therefore 3.32 times against 3.37 times, a small improvement that comes from cash rising by 100.5 rather than from earnings growth; gross debt before unamortized costs was nearly unchanged at 5,249.7 against 5,249.1. Leverage was higher at the March and June 2026 test dates (3.52 and 3.42 times net) because unrestricted cash (287.9 and 366.5) and trailing Adjusted EBITDA (1,411.3 and 1,429.6) were both lower then. On unadjusted EBITDA, which includes integration costs and unrealized gains, trailing leverage is 4.34 times gross and 3.95 times net, so the difference between the two bases, 0.68 times gross and 0.63 times net, measures how much of the credit story rests on add-backs. The add-backs fell from 365.1 in FY2025 to 124.4 in nine months 2026, which supports management's view that integration costs are winding down (Q3 10-Q page:49), but the "other adjustments, net" line is still 11.5 in nine months 2026 against (5.0) in nine months 2025 (Q3 release page:11).

facts.label: Coverage
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 4.81 times over the trailing twelve months and covered interest and financing expense, net 4.50 times. Interest and financing expense, net for nine months 2026 was 239.5, 3.1% lower than 247.1 a year earlier (Q3 10-Q page:50), even though the term loan margin rose to 2.75% from 2.25% at the refinancing (Q3 10-Q page:16; 10-K page:156); the swaps fix the rate on 500.0 of the term loans and one of them ends December 31, 2026. Cash interest paid of 200.4 was below the expense of 239.5 for nine months; non-cash amortization of debt discount and issuance costs of 21.5 (Q3 10-Q page:6) explains part, and the timing of semi-annual coupons in April and October (10-K page:159, page:160) is a consistent but unstated explanation for the rest, which is an inference. These ratios are not the covenant measure.

facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: Operating cash flow from continuing operations was 625.3 for nine months 2026, up 148.1. The company attributes this to improved earnings excluding non-cash charges of 80.1 and an increase in cash provided by trade payables and accruals of 141.1, partly offset by larger uses for prepaid assets, receivables and inventories (Q3 10-Q page:58). A payables-driven gain can reverse. Receivables absorbed 163.5 in nine months 2026 against 133.4, and cash paid for income taxes rose to 112.0 from 56.8. Free cash flow was 319.6 against 203.4. Dividends of 131.2 and buybacks of 70.1 took 201.3 of it, leaving 118.3, about 37% of free cash flow, while cash rose by 100.5. The adjusted free cash flow of 602.9 adds back 146.3 of acquisition, integration and restructuring cash costs and 101.8 of integration capital expenditure among other items (Q3 release page:12), so the gap between free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow of 283.3 is itself management-defined. Purchases of property, plant and equipment and intangibles were 305.7 for nine months 2026, 5.8% of net sales; the outlook's "Base CAPEX" of 4% of net sales is a separate management measure, so the two are not directly comparable.

facts.label: Liquidity
facts.text: Cash of 477.2 plus revolver availability of 586.6 gives 1,063.8, against current portion of long-term debt of 74.4 and nine-month cash interest of 200.4. The revolver matures February 2030, so no facility expires within twelve months, but the springing maturity condition is not stated and could shorten it. The company states that it does not expect to generate sufficient cash from operations to repay at maturity the entirety of its debt and so depends on refinancing (Q3 10-Q page:51). The revolver is assumed undrawn because the filing speaks of "undrawn availability" and no revolver borrowing line appears in the financing cash flows; that is an inference.

facts.label: Earnings quality and definitions
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA is defined by management as net income from continuing operations before interest, taxes and depreciation and amortization, adjusted for acquisition, integration and restructuring expenses, stock-based compensation, unrealized gains and losses on foreign exchange and commodity forwards, loss on disposal of property, plant and equipment, debt modification losses, purchase accounting and other adjustments (Q3 10-Q page:43). Four points matter. First, the integration add-back of 91.2 for nine months 2026 is larger than the statement line of 47.5 because 43.7 of integration cost sits in cost of sales (Q3 release page:11, page:12). Second, Q3 2026 operating income of 248.9 includes other operating income of 28.0, of which 27.6 is unrealized gains on commodity forwards (Q3 10-Q page:47); Adjusted EBITDA removes 26.1 of unrealized gains, against unrealized gains of 27.6 in Q3 2026 and 1.8 in Q3 2025 in operating income, so part of the rise in operating income is a mark-to-market swing. Third, depreciation and amortization fell to 146.3 from 163.1 in Q3 2026, mainly because amortization of customer lists and definite-lived trade names fell to 30.1 from 56.1 (Q3 release page:12), which lifts net income without any cash effect. Fourth, FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA excluded insurance proceeds of 47.3 and added back an intangible asset impairment of 35.6 (10-K page:86). The effective tax rate was 28.4% for nine months 2026 against 36.4% (Q3 10-Q page:50).

facts.text: The readiness review described the difference between the debt before unamortized costs in the Q3 release (5,249.7) and the fair-value table total (5,017.5), 232.2, as debt the Q3 report does not itemize. That wording is too strong. It is still not decomposed in the Q3 10-Q, and the gap about finance leases, other debt and the revolver balance stands, but the 232.2 should not be read as unitemized debt.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Primo Brands operates one segment: a vertically integrated North American branded water business with retail distribution to more than 200,000 outlets and a recurring direct-to-consumer arm made up of Direct Delivery, Exchange and Refill. Revenue is split about evenly between regional spring water and everything else, premium water is the fastest-growing category, and one retail customer accounted for about a fifth of FY2025 net sales, which is the main concentration disclosed. Margin is exposed to freight, materials and tariff costs, and integration costs are fading but still sit in cost of sales. There is no pending sale, merger or acquisition in the sources. The transactions that matter to a creditor are historical or financial: the November 2024 combination of BlueTriton and Primo Water, the March 2026 term loan refinancing, a series of sponsor secondary offerings with company repurchases alongside them, and a new repurchase program approved on November 3, 2026. The sponsor affiliate held about 32.0% of voting power in February 2026 and the stockholders agreement gives it approval rights over large dividends, share repurchases and added debt above a stated leverage level while it holds at least 30% of the Class A shares; its present holding after the August 2026 sale is not disclosed, so those rights may or may not apply. Documented actions show cash returns to shareholders and a pre-combination dividend to the sponsor, and no priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release in 2026, although the February 2025 exchange offers stripped covenants and guarantees from original notes that were not tendered. Behaviour is therefore read as mixed on the evidence available, not as extraction-oriented or creditor-adverse. Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility cannot be separated without the credit agreement, the indentures and the stockholders agreement, none of which is in the pack.

The transactions that matter to a creditor are historical or financial: the November 2024 combination of BlueTriton and Primo Water, the March 2026 term loan refinancing, a series of sponsor secondary offerings with company repurchases alongside them, and a new repurchase program approved on November 3, 2026. The sponsor affiliate held about 32.0% of voting power in February 2026 and the stockholders agreement gives it approval rights over large dividends, share repurchases and added debt above a stated leverage level while it holds at least 30% of the Class A shares; its present holding after the August 2026 sale is not disclosed, so those rights may or may not apply. Documented actions show cash returns to shareholders and a pre-combination dividend to the sponsor, and no priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release in 2026, although the February 2025 exchange offers stripped covenants and guarantees from original notes that were not tendered. Behaviour is therefore read as mixed on the evidence available, not as extraction-oriented or creditor-adverse. Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility cannot be separated without the credit agreement, the indentures and the stockholders agreement, none of which is in the pack.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: There is no pending acquisition, disposal or merger in the sources, and no new bond issue in 2026. The one financing transaction in the period is the Fifth Amendment of March 31, 2026, which refinanced term loans then outstanding at 3,067.6 into new term loans of 3,090.0 maturing in March 2031, repricing the SOFR margin to 2.75% from 2.25%, while the revolving credit facility of 750.0 is described as maturing in February 2030 subject to a springing maturity whose condition is not stated (Q3 10-Q page:16, page:17; 10-K page:156). The company recorded a loss on modification and extinguishment of debt of 17.7 in nine months 2026. The three note series, the 3.875% Senior Secured Notes due October 31, 2028, the 4.375% Senior Secured Notes due April 30, 2029 and the 6.250% Senior Notes due April 1, 2029, date from exchange offers completed with new indentures on February 12, 2025, in which the issuers co-issued new notes for the original Primo Water Holdings and Triton Water Holdings series; holders who did not tender kept original notes whose covenants were largely removed (10-K page:158 to page:160). Ownership transactions are the other group. The November 8, 2024 combination of BlueTriton and Primo Water was accounted for as an acquisition of Primo Water with BlueTriton as accounting acquirer (10-K page:146). The sponsor affiliate sold shares in secondary offerings in March 2025 and May 2025 totalling 99,250,000 shares and again on August 7, 2026, when it sold 20,000,000 shares at 24.37 a share and the company, using cash on hand, bought 410,340 shares from it for about 10.0 while receiving no offering proceeds (10-K page:46; Q3 10-Q page:19). The status of each is closed. After quarter end, on November 3, 2026, the board declared a dividend of 0.12 a share and approved a new repurchase program of up to 300.0 that replaces a program with 40.8 left (Q3 10-Q page:39); this is announced and unexecuted. The company also sold production facilities held for sale for gross proceeds of 41.3 in nine months 2026 and had agreements after December 31, 2025 to sell further facilities for combined proceeds of 38.3 (Q3 10-Q page:15; 10-K page:191). The nature of the nine-month acquisitions of 48.0 shown in investing cash flow is not described in the sources and stays Insufficient Information. The effect of any of these on leverage is limited: the refinancing raised principal by 22.4, the repurchases consume cash that would otherwise reduce net debt, and the facility sale proceeds are modest against total debt. How the company would fund a larger repurchase while keeping leverage near the level in the financial base is not stated.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Primo Brands Corporation's fundamental credit view is moderately cautious: a scaled branded-water business with improving cash flow and ample liquidity, but leverage that rests heavily on management add-backs and a cluster of note maturities in 2028 and 2029. The strongest support is USD 1,063.8 million of liquidity at 2026-09-30, USD 625.3 million of operating cash flow in nine months 2026 and a term loan now due in March 2031. The weakest point is that trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,436.1 million is slightly below year-end, leaving leverage at 3.66x gross and 3.32x net, or 4.34x gross before add-backs, while shareholder returns continue. Three things decide the outcome: how freight and materials costs are passed through, whether shareholder returns are balanced against deleveraging, and the refinancing of the 2028 and 2029 notes.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Primo Brands earned slightly less per dollar of revenue in 2026 even as revenue grew. Net sales for nine months 2026 were USD 5,243.3 million, up 2.6%, but Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,102.0 million, down 1.0%, and the margin was 21.0% against 21.8%. Cost of sales grew faster than sales on freight, materials and depreciation, and the filings flag tariffs and supply chain disruption as continuing cost risks. Q3 2026 was better: net sales rose 3.1% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.6% to USD 411.0 million [Financial base, Business context].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is moderate on the company's definition and materially higher without add-backs. Total debt before unamortized costs was USD 5,249.7 million at 2026-09-30 and unrestricted cash was USD 477.2 million, giving net debt of USD 4,772.5 million. On trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,436.1 million that is 3.66x gross and 3.32x net. On trailing EBITDA of USD 1,209.1 million before USD 227.0 million of add-backs it is 4.34x gross and 3.95x net. Add-backs are shrinking as integration costs wind down, from USD 365.1 million in FY2025 to USD 124.4 million in nine months 2026, but they are still management-defined. Net leverage was 3.37x at year-end 2025 and 3.32x at 2026-09-30, so the improvement is small and came mainly from a USD 100.5 million rise in cash [Financial base].

facts.text: Shareholder returns compete with deleveraging. Dividends of USD 131.2 million and buybacks of USD 70.1 million took USD 201.3 million, 63% of nine-month free cash flow. Over the trailing twelve months dividends and buybacks of USD 364.1 million were about equal to free cash flow of USD 362.1 million. The board approved a new repurchase program of up to USD 300.0 million on 2026-11-03 and declared a dividend of USD 0.12 a share. The sponsor affiliate sold 20,000,000 shares in August 2026 and the company bought back 410,340 shares from it for about USD 10.0 million. The stockholders agreement gives the sponsor approval rights over large dividends, most repurchases and debt that would take total net leverage above 3.5x while it holds at least 30% of the shares; its holding after August 2026 is not disclosed, so whether those rights still apply is unknown [Financial base, Business context].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is ample and the maturity wall sits later than the term loan. Liquidity of USD 1,063.8 million is USD 477.2 million of cash plus USD 586.6 million of revolver availability after USD 163.4 million of letters of credit, with the revolver assumed undrawn because the filing speaks of undrawn availability. The term loan was refinanced to March 2031 at a SOFR margin of 2.75%, up from 2.25%. The derived ladder puts USD 532.3 million due in 2028 and USD 1,490.2 million in 2029, mainly the 3.875%, 4.375% and 6.250% notes, against USD 2,943.2 million in 2031. The revolver matures in February 2030 with a springing maturity whose condition is not stated, and the company says it does not expect operating cash flow to repay all debt at maturity [Financial base].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Scale and brands: a vertically integrated North American network of more than 50 production facilities and more than 200 depots, with regional spring water, purified water and premium water brands, and growth in premium water of 31.7% for nine months 2026 [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Liquidity: USD 1,063.8 million at 2026-09-30, no facility expiring within twelve months, and a term loan refinanced to March 2031 [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Cash generation: free cash flow of USD 319.6 million for nine months 2026, up from USD 203.4 million, and trailing cash interest cover of 4.81x on Adjusted EBITDA [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Falling add-backs: USD 124.4 million for nine months 2026 against USD 262.5 million, as integration winds down [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Creditor protections: first lien security for the term loan and secured notes, a sponsor veto on leverage-increasing debt while the holding is at least 30%, and no priming, uptiering or collateral release in 2026 [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Management states the objective of reducing net leverage [Management Language; Business context].

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a moderately cautious view is that liquidity is 1,063.8, free cash flow is 319.6 against 203.4, add-backs have fallen to 124.4 from 262.5, net leverage has fallen from 3.52x in March to 3.32x, the company-reported ratings carry a positive outlook at one agency by column order, and management left Adjusted Free Cash Flow guidance of 790 to 810 unchanged. If integration costs keep falling and freight costs ease, trailing Adjusted EBITDA could rise while shareholder returns stay within free cash flow. What would make that case win: fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of at least 363.0, the amount implied by the low end of guidance, adjusted free cash flow in the implied range of 187.1 to 207.1, repurchases staying below free cash flow, and early refinancing of the 2028 notes.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: Downside chain with observable triggers. Initiating condition: a freight, materials or tariff cost shock that pricing does not offset. First operational break: gross margin falling below the 29.9% of nine months 2026. Financial transmission: lower Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow while the dividend of 0.12 a share per quarter and the repurchase program continue. Leverage consequence: with net debt unchanged at 4,772.5, a fall of about 5% in trailing Adjusted EBITDA takes net leverage to 3.5x (Calculations), the level the stockholders agreement summary uses as a test. Liquidity and refinancing consequence: revolver drawings above the assumed nil balance would reduce liquidity below 1,063.8, and lenders would face the 3.875% notes due October 31, 2028 and the April 2029 notes with weaker cover. Triggers to watch: quarterly gross margin, add-backs, the revolver balance, repurchase pace against free cash flow, the sponsor's disclosed holding, and the covenant certificate when obtainable.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven documents cover the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases through the third quarter of 2026, which is enough to start all four planned analyses, with stated limits. | Medium | No credit agreement, indenture or presentation is supplied, so debt terms and covenant headroom rest on filing summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The annual report lists debt by instrument, but the quarterly reports print only a fair-value debt table, and the annual maturity ladder predates the March 2026 term loan refinancing. | The maturity wall must be rebuilt from the refinancing terms, and finance leases and other debt at the latest quarter are not itemized. | High |

| The revolver covenants are printed as a first lien net leverage test and an interest coverage test, but no reported ratio or headroom is printed. | Covenant headroom cannot be measured; only the stated levels and the compliance statement are available. | High |

| Credit ratings and outlooks are printed in the latest quarterly report even though the run context leaves ratings blank. | The filing figures are usable as an issuer-reported rating record, not as an independent rating source. | Medium |

| A securities class action, a consumer class action and a spring-water labelling class action are disclosed, with no estimate of possible loss beyond amounts accrued. | These are unquantified contingent claims that later work must carry as limits. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The supplied set supports the requested work with limitations. All four selected consumers are assessed as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, none is CONDITIONAL and none is BLOCKED. The audited annual report, the three quarterly reports and the three releases identify one registrant, Primo Brands Corporation, report one segment in USD, and cover FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026 up to the cutoff. Four limitations bind. First, the pack holds no executed financing document, so covenant levels, guarantor lists, security and the springing maturity condition rest on filing descriptions. Second, the annual debt table and maturity ladder describe the position before the March 2026 refinancing, and the latest quarterly report gives only a fair-value debt table, so a current instrument-level debt schedule must be assembled from several sources. Third, three class actions are disclosed without an estimate of possible loss beyond amounts accrued. Fourth, text extraction was not reviewed for fidelity, and charts, images and the earnings presentations referred to in the releases are not in the pack. None of these stops a consumer from starting, and each is carried forward.
### Per-source assessment
| Source | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Version relationship |

| 10-K FY2025 | Primo Brands Corporation and wholly-owned subsidiaries, one reportable segment (`page:184`); the accounting acquirer for the 2024 combination was BlueTriton (`page:84`), so FY2023 reflects only BlueTriton and Primo Water is included from November 9, 2024 (`page:84`) | Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 with 2024 and 2023 comparatives; USD millions; audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (`page:124`), with the FY2023 statements audited by Ernst & Young LLP (`page:125`) | Only full-year source; controls FY2025 and the December 31, 2025 balance sheet; the debt table and ladder are as of that date |

| 10-Q Q1 2026 | Same registrant; same single segment | Three months ended March 31, 2026 versus 2025; unaudited; first filing after the March 31, 2026 term loan amendment (`page:14` and `page:15`) | Separate active source |
| 10-Q Q2 2026 | Same registrant | Three and six months ended June 30, 2026; unaudited | Separate active source |

| 10-Q Q3 2026 | Same registrant; no operations outside North America (`page:11`) | Three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 versus 2025; balance sheet versus December 31, 2025; unaudited | Latest filed statements; controls Q3 2026 and nine-month facts |

| EX-99.1 Q1, Q2, Q3 2026 | Same consolidated perimeter; releases state a new comparable net sales basis that excludes the exited Eastern Canadian operations and the exited US Office Coffee Services business (Q3 release `page:13`) | Quarter and, in the Q3 release, nine-month and trailing figures; non-GAAP reconciliations | Each release is a separate active source; the filed report controls where both state a fact |
### Entity and perimeter map

The registrant is Primo Brands Corporation (cover, `page:1` of each report). The notes name different entities for debt. Under the First Lien Credit Agreement, Primo Brands is the parent borrower, Triton Water Holdings, Inc. and Primo Water Holdings Inc. are borrowers, and Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. is term loan administrative agent and collateral agent (10-Q Q3 `page:16`). The three series of senior notes are co-issued by Primo Water Holdings Inc. and Triton Water Holdings, Inc., described as indirect, wholly owned subsidiaries (10-K `page:158`). The 3.875% Senior Notes are described as secured and "guaranteed by the Company and substantially all of the Company's wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries" (10-K `page:160`), and the 6.250% Senior Notes as guaranteed "by the Company and certain subsidiaries" (10-K `page:159`). Security is described in the 10-K MD&A: the term loans are secured by a first-priority lien on substantially all of the issuers' and guarantors' current and fixed assets (`page:95`), the two secured note series rank pari passu with the credit agreement liens (`page:98`) and the 6.250% Senior Notes are "senior unsecured obligations" (`page:99`). No separate co-issuer or guarantor financial statements were located in the pack (searches for guarantor summarized financial information found none), so the consolidated statements are the only perimeter available. Whether the consolidated figures equal the restricted group is an unresolved distinction and is logged as a gap.

The 2024 combination makes FY2024 and FY2023 comparatives only partly like-for-like with FY2025 (10-K `page:84`). The context names FY2025 as the prior period, which sits wholly after the combination.
### Strongest usable coverage

- Statements. The Q3 10-Q carries the balance sheet (`page:4`), statements of operations (`page:5`), cash flows with cash paid for interest and income taxes (`page:6` and `page:7`) and equity (`page:7`). The 10-K carries the audited FY2025 statements (`page:126` onward).

- Debt. The 10-K debt note prints the instrument table (Term Loans, 6.250%, 3.875% and 4.375% Senior Notes, Revolving Credit Facility, finance leases, other, unamortized costs), principal maturities by year, and terms (`page:154` to `page:162`). The Q3 10-Q describes the March 31, 2026 refinancing into a term loan of $3,090.0 million maturing in March 2031 (`page:16`), the covenants (`page:17`), a fair-value debt table (`page:30`), $163.4 million of letters of credit (`page:38`), $750.0 million of revolving commitments (`page:51`) and credit ratings (`page:53`).

- Non-GAAP. The Q3 release reconciles net income from continuing operations to Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter and nine months (`page:11`), free cash flow (`page:12`) and the net leverage ratio build (`page:13` and `page:14`). The 10-K reconciles FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA (`page:86`).
- Narrative and outlook. The releases print a full-year outlook (Q3 release `page:2`) and the 10-Q MD&A gives drivers and liquidity (`page:40` to `page:54`).
- Contingencies and subsequent events. Note 14 sets out the litigation (`page:34` to `page:38`) and Note 16 the dividend and new repurchase program (`page:39`).

This supports CP-1 (document and financial read), CP-1A (financials and credit metrics inputs), CP-2 (debt structure, maturities and liquidity) and CP-5 (transaction and event read-through) at the located level.
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations

1. Debt table and ladder are stale for the term loan. The 10-K ladder shows 2028 at "3,535.2" and a total of "5,078.3" (`page:155`), and the term loans then matured March 31, 2028 (`page:156`). The Q3 10-Q says the refinancing facility "will mature in March 2031" and amortizes 1.00% per annum (`page:16`). The 10-K ladder therefore cannot be used as the current wall. The Q3 report prints no new ladder (search of the Q3 10-Q for "maturities" found none), so a current ladder is a downstream derivation from the 10-K senior note maturities and the Q3 term loan terms.

2. Finance leases, other debt and revolver balance are not itemized at September 30, 2026. The Q3 fair-value table totals "5,017.5" (`page:30`) while the release prints "Total debt, excluding unamortized debt costs and discounts" of "5,249.7" (Q3 release `page:14`). The difference is tied out in `## Calculations` and is not described in the Q3 report. The Q3 10-Q does not state a revolver drawn balance; the 10-K table shows the revolver as "—" at December 31, 2025 (`page:154`) and the MD&A says the company had "access to $750.0 million of revolving loan commitments (without giving effect to $163.4 million of outstanding letters of credit)" (10-Q Q3 `page:51`).

3. No reported covenant ratio. The Revolving Credit Facility requires "a first lien net leverage ratio of less than or equal to 5.00 to 1.00" and "a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.00 to 1.00" (10-Q Q3 `page:17`), and the company states it "was in compliance with all covenants" (`page:18`). Neither the first lien net leverage nor the interest coverage ratio as computed under the credit agreement is printed. The release's net leverage ratio of 3.32x (Q3 release `page:14`) is a management measure on total debt less unrestricted cash over TTM Adjusted EBITDA and is not stated to be the covenant definition.

4. Executed documents not supplied. The 10-K exhibit index lists the credit agreement and indentures by incorporation (`page:116` to `page:118`) and the pack contains none of their text. The springing maturity on the revolver is described only as "subject to a springing maturity based on conditions set forth in the Amended Credit Agreement" (10-Q Q3 `page:17`); the condition is not stated.

5. Management measures versus filings. Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow, adjusted free cash flow and net leverage are non-GAAP and appear in the releases and the 10-Q MD&A; the filed statements control GAAP facts. The TTM Adjusted EBITDA of 1,436.1 combines a FY2025 figure, which the 10-K also prints (`page:86`), with nine-month figures from the Q3 release. For nine months 2026 the bridge runs from EBITDA of "977.6" to Adjusted EBITDA of "1,102.0", and its largest item is acquisition, integration and restructuring expenses of "91.2" (Q3 release `page:11`).

6. Comparability. The releases restate the 2025 comparison base to exclude exited operations (Q3 release `page:13`), and the discontinued operations line in 2025 (net loss of "(32.6)" for nine months 2025, Q3 10-Q `page:5`) has no 2026 counterpart. Prior-period amounts "have been reclassified to conform with the 2026 presentation" (Q3 10-Q `page:10`) without a reclassification schedule in the text read.

7. Contingent claims without estimates. The securities class action, the consumer class action and the Patane spring-water labelling class action are disclosed in Note 14 (`page:34` to `page:38`). The company states it is "unable to reasonably estimate the amount or range of possible loss, if any, in excess of the amounts accrued" (`page:34`). The Patane parties scheduled a second mediation for November 19, 2026 (`page:38`), after the cutoff, so any outcome is outside this pack.

8. Not supplied. Earnings presentations (the releases refer to a supplemental presentation on the company website, which is not in the pack), executed legal documents, market quotes, peers, valuation inputs, deal terms and a discrete Q4 2025 quarter. A Q4 2025 figure would be a downstream derivation from the 10-K and interim sources, not a source.

9. Extraction only. All seven files are text conversions; charts and images are not inspected, and successful extraction is not a fidelity review. Not every chunk was read line by line in this review; the chunks read are those cited.
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | Status | Basis | Carried limitations |
| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Filed statements, notes, MD&A and releases for FY2025 and three 2026 quarters are present and located | Limitations 4, 6, 8, 9 |
| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements, non-GAAP reconciliations, cash interest paid and cash taxes paid are present for quarter, nine months and FY2025 | Limitations 3, 5, 6, 8, 9 |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Instrument table and ladder at December 31, 2025, refinancing terms, covenant levels, letters of credit, revolver commitments and ratings at September 30, 2026 | Limitations 1, 2, 3, 4, 7; no executed debt documents; guarantor and restricted-group perimeter unresolved |

| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Subsequent-event disclosures (dividend and new repurchase program, Q3 10-Q `page:39`), the August 2026 secondary offering by Triton Water Equity Holdings (`page:61`), the Stock Purchase Agreement exhibit (`page:63`) and outlook | Limitations 4, 7, 8; the Stock Purchase Agreement text is not supplied |
No selected consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED on source grounds. These statuses do not assert that downstream analysis is complete or that any model input contract is accepted.
### Conflicts and checks between sources

No factual conflict between a filing and a release was found in the items compared. The Q3 release balance sheet matches the Q3 10-Q balance sheet line for line on the lines read (total assets "10,828.0", total liabilities "7,779.3", `page:4` of the 10-Q and `page:9` of the release). The release's "Unrestricted cash" of "477.2" differs from the balance sheet's "477.4" only by the "$0.2 million" of restricted cash that the release footnote and the 10-Q MD&A both state (Q3 release `page:14`; 10-Q `page:51`). The release and 10-Q Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter agree at "411.0" (release `page:11`; 10-Q `page:44`).
### Context fields that are blank

Ratings are blank in the context, but the Q3 10-Q prints ratings (`page:53`): Corporate / Family "B1" and "BB-", Senior Secured "Ba3" and "BB", Senior Unsecured "B3" and "B", with the row "Outlook Positive Neutral". The agency columns are read from the table header order (Moody's, then Standard and Poor's); the extraction does not show cell alignment, so the pairing of outlook to agency is by order only. These are company-reported statements as of September 30, 2026, not independent rating documents. Borrower, parent and guarantor fields are blank in the context while the filings name borrowers and guarantors (see the entity map).
## Calculations
No new analytical calculation is performed in this module. The tie-outs below test source consistency only and use figures copied from the cited sources. Units are USD millions.
| Check | Inputs | Result | Source locators |

| Total debt on the balance sheet | Current portion of long-term debt 74.4 plus long-term debt, less current portion 5,087.7 | 5,162.1, equal to "Total debt" of 5,162.1 in the release | 10-Q Q3 `page:4`; Q3 release `page:14` |
| Debt before unamortized costs | Total debt 5,162.1 plus unamortized debt costs and discounts 87.6 | 5,249.7, equal to the release figure | Q3 release `page:14` |
| Net debt | 5,249.7 less unrestricted cash 477.2 | 4,772.5, equal to the release figure | Q3 release `page:14` |
| TTM Adjusted EBITDA | FY2025 1,446.8 less nine months 2025 1,112.7 plus nine months 2026 1,102.0 | 1,436.1, equal to the release figure | 10-K `page:86`; Q3 release `page:11` and `page:14` |
| Net leverage ratio | 4,772.5 divided by 1,436.1 | 3.32x to two decimals, equal to the release | Q3 release `page:14` |

| Debt not in the fair-value table | Release debt before unamortized costs 5,249.7 less fair-value table carrying total 5,017.5 | 232.2; the Q3 report does not itemize it | 10-Q Q3 `page:30`; Q3 release `page:14` |

| Term loan principal roll | Refinanced principal 3,090.0 less "Repayment of Term Loans" of 7.7 in Q2 2026 and 7.8 in Q3 2026 | 3,090.0 less 15.5 is 3,074.5, equal to the term loan carrying value in the fair-value table; 1.00% per annum on 3,090.0 is 7.725 per quarter, consistent with the two payments | 10-Q Q3 `page:16`, `page:30`, `page:7`; 10-Q Q2 `page:7` |
The tie-outs show the release net leverage build reproduces from sources in the pack. They do not validate the Adjusted EBITDA adjustments and do not show the covenant ratio.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation | Citation |

| Executed credit agreement, Fifth Amendment, indentures and other legal documents not supplied (context states none) | Medium | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the executed documents for covenant definitions, springing maturity condition, guarantor lists, baskets and change-of-control terms | 10-K `page:116` to `page:118`; 10-Q Q3 `page:17` |

| No post-refinancing maturity ladder in a filing; 10-K ladder predates the March 2026 refinancing | Medium | CP-2 | Rebuild downstream from note maturities and the Q3 term loan terms, labelled as derived | 10-K `page:155`; 10-Q Q3 `page:16` |

| Finance leases, other debt and revolver drawn balance at September 30, 2026 not itemized | Medium | CP-2, CP-1A | Use the December 31, 2025 table as the last itemized view and label the 232.2 residual as unitemized | 10-Q Q3 `page:30`; 10-K `page:154` and `page:155` |

| Reported covenant ratios and headroom not printed | Medium | CP-2 | Not supplied; compute a management-basis proxy only and label that it is not the covenant definition | 10-Q Q3 `page:17`, `page:18` |
| Guarantor and restricted-group financial information not located | Medium | CP-2 | Supply guarantor disclosures if the restricted perimeter matters | 10-K `page:158` to `page:160` |
| Earnings presentations not in the pack | Low | CP-1, CP-1A | Not supplied; the releases and filings cover the reported facts | Q3 release `page:3` |

| Ratings, market quotes, peers, valuation inputs, deal terms blank in context | Medium | CP-2, CP-5 | Not supplied in the context; ratings are printed by the company in the 10-Q | context; 10-Q Q3 `page:53` |
| Discrete Q4 2025 quarter not supplied | Low | CP-1A | Derive downstream if needed; FY2025 less nine months 2025 | 10-K `page:126` |
| Estimates of possible loss beyond amounts accrued for the disclosed class actions not given | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | None available in the pack | 10-Q Q3 `page:34` to `page:38` |
| Prior-period reclassification detail not located | Low | CP-1A | Check the statements note in the 10-K against the 10-Q comparatives | 10-Q Q3 `page:10` |
| Text-only extraction; images and charts not inspected; fidelity not reviewed | Low | All | Record as a parse limitation | All sources |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-1. Carry forward: the single registrant and one segment with co-issuer and guarantor entities named only in the debt notes; the pre-refinancing basis of the 10-K debt table and ladder; the absence of executed financing documents and of a reported covenant ratio; the company-reported ratings in the Q3 10-Q; the three disclosed class actions without loss estimates; and the non-GAAP basis of Adjusted EBITDA and net leverage. ### Financial base view

Primo Brands Corporation reports as one registrant with one segment, so the base is a single consolidated set of statements rather than a segment mosaic. Through nine months 2026, net sales were 5,243.3, up 2.6% on 5,109.9, and Adjusted EBITDA was 1,102.0, down 1.0% from 1,112.7, because cost of sales grew faster than sales on freight and materials costs (Q3 10-Q `page:49`). Q3 2026 was better than the first half: net sales rose 3.1% to 1,821.0, Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.6% to 411.0 and the margin was 22.6% against 22.9% a year earlier. EBITDA before add-backs rose much faster than Adjusted EBITDA (396.9 against 313.1 in Q3) because lower integration costs (add-back of 23.7 against 88.2) and an unrealized gain of 26.1, both excluded from Adjusted EBITDA, flowed through, and the total add-backs shrank to 14.1 in Q3 2026 from 91.4 a year earlier. Trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 1,436.1 gives gross leverage of 3.66 times and net leverage of 3.32 times on the company's definition; on EBITDA before add-backs of 1,209.1 the ratios are 4.34 and 3.95 times. Cash paid for interest of 298.7 over the trailing twelve months is covered 4.81 times by Adjusted EBITDA. Operating cash flow was 625.3 for nine months against 477.2, with payables and accruals contributing 141.1 of the 148.1 improvement, partly offset by other working capital lines; a payables-driven gain can reverse. Liquidity of 1,063.8 is cash of 477.2 plus revolver commitments of 750.0 less 163.4 of letters of credit. The March 2026 refinancing moved the term loan to March 2031, so the nearest large maturities are the 3.875% notes in October 2028 and the 4.375% and 6.250% notes in April 2029. Four limits bind: Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure with large add-backs, covenant ratios are not printed, finance leases, other debt and the revolver balance are not itemized at September 30, 2026, and the maturity ladder after the refinancing is derived, not filed.

### Latest quarter and events to the cutoff

- Financing. The Fifth Amendment of March 31, 2026 refinanced term loans of 3,067.6 into 3,090.0 maturing March 2031, a net principal increase of 22.4, with a loss on modification and extinguishment of debt of 17.7 in nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:16`, `page:17`). No financing event on debt occurred in Q3 2026; term loan repayments were 7.8 (Q3 10-Q `page:7`).

- Equity. On August 7, 2026 the sponsor affiliate Triton Water Equity Holdings sold 20,000,000 shares at 24.37 a share in a secondary offering, and the company bought back 410,340 shares from it for about 10.0 funded from cash; the company received no offering proceeds (Q3 10-Q `page:19`, `page:61`).

- After quarter end. On November 3, 2026 the board declared a dividend of 0.12 a share payable December 4, 2026 and approved a new share repurchase program of up to 300.0, replacing the existing program that had 40.8 of authorization left at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:39`).

- Outlook. The Q3 release expects net sales at the midpoint of the previous 2% to 4% growth range and Adjusted EBITDA at the lower end of the previous 1,465 to 1,515 range, with base capital expenditure of 4% of net sales and Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 790 to 810 unchanged (Q3 release `page:2`). In May 2026 the Adjusted EBITDA range was widened from 1,485 to 1,515 to 1,465 to 1,515 (Q1 release `page:2`), and in August it was reaffirmed (Q2 release `page:2`). These are attributed management claims and are not reconciled to GAAP (Q3 release `page:6`).

- Restructuring. Management expected aggregate restructuring charges of about 75.0 to 100.0 in connection with the 2024 combination, and no further cash termination benefits are expected (Q3 10-Q `page:23`).
### Interpretation
#### Leverage

Net debt fell to 4,772.5 at September 30, 2026 from 4,872.4 at December 31, 2025, a decrease of 99.9, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA fell to 1,436.1 from 1,446.8. Net leverage on the company's definition was therefore 3.32 times against 3.37 times, a small improvement that comes from cash rising by 100.5 rather than from earnings growth; gross debt before unamortized costs was nearly unchanged at 5,249.7 against 5,249.1. Leverage was higher at the March and June 2026 test dates (3.52 and 3.42 times net) because unrestricted cash (287.9 and 366.5) and trailing Adjusted EBITDA (1,411.3 and 1,429.6) were both lower then. On unadjusted EBITDA, which includes integration costs and unrealized gains, trailing leverage is 4.34 times gross and 3.95 times net, so the difference between the two bases, 0.68 times gross and 0.63 times net, measures how much of the credit story rests on add-backs. The add-backs fell from 365.1 in FY2025 to 124.4 in nine months 2026, which supports management's view that integration costs are winding down (Q3 10-Q `page:49`), but the "other adjustments, net" line is still 11.5 in nine months 2026 against (5.0) in nine months 2025 (Q3 release `page:11`).
#### Coverage

Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 4.81 times over the trailing twelve months and covered interest and financing expense, net 4.50 times. Interest and financing expense, net for nine months 2026 was 239.5, 3.1% lower than 247.1 a year earlier (Q3 10-Q `page:50`), even though the term loan margin rose to 2.75% from 2.25% at the refinancing (Q3 10-Q `page:16`; 10-K `page:156`); the swaps fix the rate on 500.0 of the term loans and one of them ends December 31, 2026. Cash interest paid of 200.4 was below the expense of 239.5 for nine months; non-cash amortization of debt discount and issuance costs of 21.5 (Q3 10-Q `page:6`) explains part, and the timing of semi-annual coupons in April and October (10-K `page:159`, `page:160`) is a consistent but unstated explanation for the rest, which is an inference. These ratios are not the covenant measure.
#### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow from continuing operations was 625.3 for nine months 2026, up 148.1. The company attributes this to improved earnings excluding non-cash charges of 80.1 and an increase in cash provided by trade payables and accruals of 141.1, partly offset by larger uses for prepaid assets, receivables and inventories (Q3 10-Q `page:58`). A payables-driven gain can reverse. Receivables absorbed 163.5 in nine months 2026 against 133.4, and cash paid for income taxes rose to 112.0 from 56.8. Free cash flow was 319.6 against 203.4. Dividends of 131.2 and buybacks of 70.1 took 201.3 of it, leaving 118.3, about 37% of free cash flow, while cash rose by 100.5. The adjusted free cash flow of 602.9 adds back 146.3 of acquisition, integration and restructuring cash costs and 101.8 of integration capital expenditure among other items (Q3 release `page:12`), so the gap between free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow of 283.3 is itself management-defined. Purchases of property, plant and equipment and intangibles were 305.7 for nine months 2026, 5.8% of net sales; the outlook's "Base CAPEX" of 4% of net sales is a separate management measure, so the two are not directly comparable.
#### Liquidity

Cash of 477.2 plus revolver availability of 586.6 gives 1,063.8, against current portion of long-term debt of 74.4 and nine-month cash interest of 200.4. The revolver matures February 2030, so no facility expires within twelve months, but the springing maturity condition is not stated and could shorten it. The company states that it does not expect to generate sufficient cash from operations to repay at maturity the entirety of its debt and so depends on refinancing (Q3 10-Q `page:51`). The revolver is assumed undrawn because the filing speaks of "undrawn availability" and no revolver borrowing line appears in the financing cash flows; that is an inference.
#### Earnings quality and definitions

Adjusted EBITDA is defined by management as net income from continuing operations before interest, taxes and depreciation and amortization, adjusted for acquisition, integration and restructuring expenses, stock-based compensation, unrealized gains and losses on foreign exchange and commodity forwards, loss on disposal of property, plant and equipment, debt modification losses, purchase accounting and other adjustments (Q3 10-Q `page:43`). Four points matter. First, the integration add-back of 91.2 for nine months 2026 is larger than the statement line of 47.5 because 43.7 of integration cost sits in cost of sales (Q3 release `page:11`, `page:12`). Second, Q3 2026 operating income of 248.9 includes other operating income of 28.0, of which 27.6 is unrealized gains on commodity forwards (Q3 10-Q `page:47`); Adjusted EBITDA removes 26.1 of unrealized gains, against unrealized gains of 27.6 in Q3 2026 and 1.8 in Q3 2025 in operating income, so part of the rise in operating income is a mark-to-market swing. Third, depreciation and amortization fell to 146.3 from 163.1 in Q3 2026, mainly because amortization of customer lists and definite-lived trade names fell to 30.1 from 56.1 (Q3 release `page:12`), which lifts net income without any cash effect. Fourth, FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA excluded insurance proceeds of 47.3 and added back an intangible asset impairment of 35.6 (10-K `page:86`). The effective tax rate was 28.4% for nine months 2026 against 36.4% (Q3 10-Q `page:50`).
#### Capital allocation

The company paid dividends of 0.12 a share each quarter in 2026 and authorized a new 300.0 repurchase program after quarter end; its sponsor affiliate sold 20,000,000 shares in August 2026 and the company bought back 410,340 shares from it. Management states a focus on generating cash flow and reducing net leverage (Q3 release `page:1`), and repurchases of 70.1 and dividends of 131.2 in nine months 2026 sit alongside it.
### Correction to the earlier handoff

The readiness review described the difference between the debt before unamortized costs in the Q3 release (5,249.7) and the fair-value table total (5,017.5), 232.2, as debt the Q3 report does not itemize. That wording is too strong. The notes lines of the fair-value table are carried net of unamortized discounts (the 10-K states discounts of 7.5 on the 3.875% notes and 31.7 on the 4.375% notes at December 31, 2025, `page:155`), while the term loan line is principal. The 232.2 therefore mixes finance leases, other debt not in the table and note discounts. It is still not decomposed in the Q3 10-Q, and the gap about finance leases, other debt and the revolver balance stands, but the 232.2 should not be read as unitemized debt.

spans.text: ## Request

Business, ownership, transaction and governance context for Primo Brands Corp (Primo Brands Corporation, NYSE: PRMB, issuer id prmb), as of 2026-11-05. Pathway credit_snapshot, reporting currency USD, current period Q3 2026, prior period FY2025. Evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Amounts are USD millions as the filings print them. The reader question is which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor, tied to risk mechanics and credit implications. This module gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion.

The earlier handoffs set the limits this module works inside. The readiness review found one registrant and one segment with no executed financing, lease or ownership documents. The financial base set out leverage of 3.66 times gross and 3.32 times net on management Adjusted EBITDA, a March 2026 term loan refinancing, a derived 2028 and 2029 note wall, liquidity of 1,063.8, and three class actions without loss estimates beyond amounts accrued. Facts are tagged Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information. Missing evidence is never an adverse conclusion.
The run context holds no sponsor, borrower, parent, guarantor, rating or deal-term values; those are Not supplied, never zero.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Primo Brands is a scaled North American branded water company with a retail-led, partly recurring direct delivery model. A large customer, sponsor-linked holders and ongoing shareholder returns shape creditor risk more than any pending transaction. | Medium | The stockholders agreement, executed debt documents and current sponsor ownership are not in the pack, so control rights and permitted distributions rest on risk-factor summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Regional spring water was 50.0% of nine-month 2026 net sales and premium water grew 31.7%, while one customer was about 21% of FY2025 net sales. | Brand breadth supports revenue durability, but one large customer concentrates volume and pricing risk. | High |

| Costs rose on freight and materials, tariffs and supply chain disruption are flagged, and integration costs are winding down. | Margin resilience depends on cost pass-through, which the filings do not quantify. | Medium |

| A sponsor-controlled holder had about 32.0% of voting power in February 2026, holds approval rights over large dividends and added debt above 30%, and sold 20,000,000 shares in August 2026. | Whether those consent rights still apply is not disclosed, so control over distributions and leverage is unclear. | Low |

| Dividends and buybacks continue, a new 300.0 million repurchase program was approved on November 3, 2026, and a 448.6 million dividend went to the sponsor in 2024. | Shareholder returns compete with deleveraging; documented actions are mixed rather than clearly creditor-friendly or creditor-adverse. | Medium |

| Three class actions allege misleading integration statements, delivery failures and spring-water mislabelling, and the filings estimate no loss beyond amounts accrued. | Unquantified claims could affect cash and brand reputation, so they stay open limits. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

Primo Brands operates one segment: a vertically integrated North American branded water business with retail distribution to more than 200,000 outlets and a recurring direct-to-consumer arm made up of Direct Delivery, Exchange and Refill. Revenue is split about evenly between regional spring water and everything else, premium water is the fastest-growing category, and one retail customer accounted for about a fifth of FY2025 net sales, which is the main concentration disclosed. Margin is exposed to freight, materials and tariff costs, and integration costs are fading but still sit in cost of sales. There is no pending sale, merger or acquisition in the sources. The transactions that matter to a creditor are historical or financial: the November 2024 combination of BlueTriton and Primo Water, the March 2026 term loan refinancing, a series of sponsor secondary offerings with company repurchases alongside them, and a new repurchase program approved on November 3, 2026. The sponsor affiliate held about 32.0% of voting power in February 2026 and the stockholders agreement gives it approval rights over large dividends, share repurchases and added debt above a stated leverage level while it holds at least 30% of the Class A shares; its present holding after the August 2026 sale is not disclosed, so those rights may or may not apply. Documented actions show cash returns to shareholders and a pre-combination dividend to the sponsor, and no priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release in 2026, although the February 2025 exchange offers stripped covenants and guarantees from original notes that were not tendered. Behaviour is therefore read as mixed on the evidence available, not as extraction-oriented or creditor-adverse. Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility cannot be separated without the credit agreement, the indentures and the stockholders agreement, none of which is in the pack.

| Category mix | Nine-month 2026 mix: regional spring water 50.0%, purified water 31.3%, premium water 6.5%, other water 1.8%, other 10.4% (derived from the water-type table) | Analyst Interpretation | Q3 10-Q `page:48`, "Regional spring water $ 2,623.7" | Half of sales rest on regional spring brands that also face labelling litigation | Brand reputation risk is concentrated in the largest category |

| Growth driver | Premium water net sales rose 31.7% for nine months 2026; the company attributes the net sales increase to premium brands and regional spring water, partly offset by the exited US office coffee services business | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q `page:49`, "a decrease of $21.7 million related to the exited US office coffee services business" | Premium growth lifts mix, but it starts from a small base | Supports margin mix only if premium margins exceed the average, which is not disclosed |

| Direct-to-consumer | Direct Delivery, Exchange (about 26,500 retail locations) and Refill (over 23,500 stations) offer recurring revenue; management says Direct Delivery growth was ahead of its expectations in Q3 2026 | Management Language | Q3 release `page:1`, "Direct Delivery growth ahead of our expectations" | Recurring routes lift visibility, but service failures can lose customers | The Hamilton complaint alleges missed deliveries after the combination (see contingencies) |

| Pricing and promotion | Sales incentives reduce net sales; accrued sales incentive obligations were 51.1 at September 30, 2026 against 36.2 at December 31, 2025 | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q `page:12`, "accrued sales incentive obligations" | Trade spend moves net price and varies with retailer demands | Net price realisation cannot be separated from volume in the sources (Insufficient Information) |

| Cost structure | Nine-month cost of sales rose on transportation (105.9) and materials (33.0) and depreciation and amortization (26.1), partly offset by lower integration costs | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q `page:49`, "increased transportation related costs of $105.9 million" | Freight and packaging costs reach margin before pricing can respond | Gross margin fell to 29.9% from 31.1% for nine months; recovery depends on pass-through that is not quantified |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no pending acquisition, disposal or merger in the sources, and no new bond issue in 2026. The one financing transaction in the period is the Fifth Amendment of March 31, 2026, which refinanced term loans then outstanding at 3,067.6 into new term loans of 3,090.0 maturing in March 2031, repricing the SOFR margin to 2.75% from 2.25%, while the revolving credit facility of 750.0 is described as maturing in February 2030 subject to a springing maturity whose condition is not stated (Q3 10-Q `page:16`, `page:17`; 10-K `page:156`). The company recorded a loss on modification and extinguishment of debt of 17.7 in nine months 2026. The three note series, the 3.875% Senior Secured Notes due October 31, 2028, the 4.375% Senior Secured Notes due April 30, 2029 and the 6.250% Senior Notes due April 1, 2029, date from exchange offers completed with new indentures on February 12, 2025, in which the issuers co-issued new notes for the original Primo Water Holdings and Triton Water Holdings series; holders who did not tender kept original notes whose covenants were largely removed (10-K `page:158` to `page:160`). Ownership transactions are the other group. The November 8, 2024 combination of BlueTriton and Primo Water was accounted for as an acquisition of Primo Water with BlueTriton as accounting acquirer (10-K `page:146`). The sponsor affiliate sold shares in secondary offerings in March 2025 and May 2025 totalling 99,250,000 shares and again on August 7, 2026, when it sold 20,000,000 shares at 24.37 a share and the company, using cash on hand, bought 410,340 shares from it for about 10.0 while receiving no offering proceeds (10-K `page:46`; Q3 10-Q `page:19`). The status of each is closed. After quarter end, on November 3, 2026, the board declared a dividend of 0.12 a share and approved a new repurchase program of up to 300.0 that replaces a program with 40.8 left (Q3 10-Q `page:39`); this is announced and unexecuted. The company also sold production facilities held for sale for gross proceeds of 41.3 in nine months 2026 and had agreements after December 31, 2025 to sell further facilities for combined proceeds of 38.3 (Q3 10-Q `page:15`; 10-K `page:191`). The nature of the nine-month acquisitions of 48.0 shown in investing cash flow is not described in the sources and stays Insufficient Information. The effect of any of these on leverage is limited: the refinancing raised principal by 22.4, the repurchases consume cash that would otherwise reduce net debt, and the facility sale proceeds are modest against total debt. How the company would fund a larger repurchase while keeping leverage near the level in the financial base is not stated.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Primo Brands has ample liquidity, rising cash flow and a term loan due in 2031, but leverage leans on management add-backs, shareholder returns continue, and the 2028 and 2029 notes are the next refinancing test. The view is moderately cautious. | Medium | Covenant ratios, the executed credit documents, the stockholders agreement and the current sponsor holding are not supplied, so headroom and distribution limits cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Trailing Adjusted EBITDA is USD 1,436.1 million, leaving leverage at 3.66x gross and 3.32x net, or 4.34x gross and 3.95x net before add-backs of USD 227.0 million. | Leverage is moderate only on management's definition, so add-back quality is central to default risk. | High |

| Liquidity is USD 1,063.8 million, and nine-month 2026 free cash flow was USD 319.6 million against USD 203.4 million a year earlier. | Debt service looks well covered today, which supports the near-term credit. | Medium |

| Shareholder returns of USD 201.3 million took 63% of nine-month free cash flow, a new USD 300.0 million repurchase program followed, and net leverage fell only from 3.37x to 3.32x. | Cash is going to equity as much as to debt reduction, which slows deleveraging. | Medium |

| About USD 2,022.5 million of derived debt matures in 2028 and 2029, which is 40.2% of the derived ladder, against USD 2,943.2 million in 2031. | The notes carry the refinancing risk, and the company says operating cash will not repay all debt at maturity. | Medium |

| One customer was about 21% of FY2025 net sales and three class actions carry no loss estimate beyond amounts accrued. | Concentration and unquantified claims are downside risks that the sources cannot size. | Medium |
### Credit view

Primo Brands Corporation's fundamental credit view is moderately cautious: a scaled branded-water business with improving cash flow and ample liquidity, but leverage that rests heavily on management add-backs and a cluster of note maturities in 2028 and 2029. The strongest support is USD 1,063.8 million of liquidity at 2026-09-30, USD 625.3 million of operating cash flow in nine months 2026 and a term loan now due in March 2031. The weakest point is that trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,436.1 million is slightly below year-end, leaving leverage at 3.66x gross and 3.32x net, or 4.34x gross before add-backs, while shareholder returns continue. Three things decide the outcome: how freight and materials costs are passed through, whether shareholder returns are balanced against deleveraging, and the refinancing of the 2028 and 2029 notes.
### Key findings

Primo Brands earned slightly less per dollar of revenue in 2026 even as revenue grew. Net sales for nine months 2026 were USD 5,243.3 million, up 2.6%, but Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,102.0 million, down 1.0%, and the margin was 21.0% against 21.8%. Cost of sales grew faster than sales on freight, materials and depreciation, and the filings flag tariffs and supply chain disruption as continuing cost risks. Q3 2026 was better: net sales rose 3.1% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.6% to USD 411.0 million [Financial base, Business context].

Leverage is moderate on the company's definition and materially higher without add-backs. Total debt before unamortized costs was USD 5,249.7 million at 2026-09-30 and unrestricted cash was USD 477.2 million, giving net debt of USD 4,772.5 million. On trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,436.1 million that is 3.66x gross and 3.32x net. On trailing EBITDA of USD 1,209.1 million before USD 227.0 million of add-backs it is 4.34x gross and 3.95x net. Add-backs are shrinking as integration costs wind down, from USD 365.1 million in FY2025 to USD 124.4 million in nine months 2026, but they are still management-defined. Net leverage was 3.37x at year-end 2025 and 3.32x at 2026-09-30, so the improvement is small and came mainly from a USD 100.5 million rise in cash [Financial base].

Cash flow improved, but part of the gain is working capital. Operating cash flow was USD 625.3 million for nine months 2026 against USD 477.2 million, of which USD 141.1 million came from payables and accruals, which can reverse. Free cash flow was USD 319.6 million against USD 203.4 million. Cash interest paid was USD 200.4 million, and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covered trailing cash interest of USD 298.7 million 4.81x [Financial base].

Shareholder returns compete with deleveraging. Dividends of USD 131.2 million and buybacks of USD 70.1 million took USD 201.3 million, 63% of nine-month free cash flow. Over the trailing twelve months dividends and buybacks of USD 364.1 million were about equal to free cash flow of USD 362.1 million. The board approved a new repurchase program of up to USD 300.0 million on 2026-11-03 and declared a dividend of USD 0.12 a share. The sponsor affiliate sold 20,000,000 shares in August 2026 and the company bought back 410,340 shares from it for about USD 10.0 million. The stockholders agreement gives the sponsor approval rights over large dividends, most repurchases and debt that would take total net leverage above 3.5x while it holds at least 30% of the shares; its holding after August 2026 is not disclosed, so whether those rights still apply is unknown [Financial base, Business context].

Liquidity is ample and the maturity wall sits later than the term loan. Liquidity of USD 1,063.8 million is USD 477.2 million of cash plus USD 586.6 million of revolver availability after USD 163.4 million of letters of credit, with the revolver assumed undrawn because the filing speaks of undrawn availability. The term loan was refinanced to March 2031 at a SOFR margin of 2.75%, up from 2.25%. The derived ladder puts USD 532.3 million due in 2028 and USD 1,490.2 million in 2029, mainly the 3.875%, 4.375% and 6.250% notes, against USD 2,943.2 million in 2031. The revolver matures in February 2030 with a springing maturity whose condition is not stated, and the company says it does not expect operating cash flow to repay all debt at maturity [Financial base].

Security and covenants favour the secured lenders and are only partly tested. About 82.3% of debt before unamortized costs, the term loan and the two secured note series, ranks first lien, and 13.6% is the unsecured 6.250% notes (Calculations). The revolver's first lien net leverage covenant of 5.00x and interest coverage covenant of 2.00x are printed, the company states compliance, and neither reported ratio nor definition is supplied. A management-basis proxy puts first lien net leverage at 2.68x and interest coverage on the expense basis at 4.50x, which shows direction only [Financial base, Source readiness].

Business concentration and claims are unsized. One customer was about 21% of FY2025 net sales, regional spring water was 50.0% of nine-month 2026 net sales, and the same category is the subject of the Patane labelling class action. A securities class action and a consumer delivery class action are also pending, and the company estimates no loss beyond amounts accrued. Operating leases of USD 612.1 million are outside the debt figure [Business context, Financial base].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Scale and brands: a vertically integrated North American network of more than 50 production facilities and more than 200 depots, with regional spring water, purified water and premium water brands, and growth in premium water of 31.7% for nine months 2026 [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Liquidity: USD 1,063.8 million at 2026-09-30, no facility expiring within twelve months, and a term loan refinanced to March 2031 [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Cash generation: free cash flow of USD 319.6 million for nine months 2026, up from USD 203.4 million, and trailing cash interest cover of 4.81x on Adjusted EBITDA [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Falling add-backs: USD 124.4 million for nine months 2026 against USD 262.5 million, as integration winds down [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Creditor protections: first lien security for the term loan and secured notes, a sponsor veto on leverage-increasing debt while the holding is at least 30%, and no priming, uptiering or collateral release in 2026 [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Management states the objective of reducing net leverage [Management Language; Business context].

Weaknesses. Leverage depends on add-backs: 4.34x gross and 3.95x net before add-backs of USD 227.0 million against 3.66x and 3.32x after [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Margin pressure: gross margin of 29.9% against 31.1% for nine months 2026 on freight and materials costs [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Shareholder returns: USD 201.3 million of nine-month dividends and buybacks and a new USD 300.0 million program, alongside a small improvement in net leverage [Documentary Fact; Financial base]. Maturity cluster: derived USD 2,022.5 million due in 2028 and 2029, and a springing maturity on the revolver with no stated condition [Analyst Interpretation; Financial base]. Concentration: one customer at about 21% of FY2025 net sales, with no 2026 update [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Asset quality: goodwill and intangible assets of USD 6,497.3 million are 60.0% of total assets and exceed stockholders' equity of USD 3,048.7 million, so tangible equity is negative [Analyst Interpretation; Calculations]. Unquantified claims: three class actions with no estimate beyond amounts accrued [Documentary Fact; Business context]. Documentation gaps: no credit agreement, indentures or stockholders agreement, so legal capacity to distribute or add debt cannot be tested [Insufficient Information; Source readiness].
### Fundamental credit assessment

The business context handoff judged this synthesis Ready with limitations and logged the sponsor-holding and stockholders-agreement gaps, so confidence stays below High. The evidence trace holds. Each material claim in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis handoffs was matched to a located source span or to a recomputation from located figures, and the three handoffs agree on every shared figure, period and perimeter label. ### Verdict consistency

The verdicts agree across modules for every shared claim. CP-2's confidence of Medium is no higher than CP-1A's readiness judgment (Ready with limitations) allows, and its listed gaps match the inherited gaps.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a moderately cautious view is that liquidity is 1,063.8, free cash flow is 319.6 against 203.4, add-backs have fallen to 124.4 from 262.5, net leverage has fallen from 3.52x in March to 3.32x, the company-reported ratings carry a positive outlook at one agency by column order, and management left Adjusted Free Cash Flow guidance of 790 to 810 unchanged. If integration costs keep falling and freight costs ease, trailing Adjusted EBITDA could rise while shareholder returns stay within free cash flow. What would make that case win: fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of at least 363.0, the amount implied by the low end of guidance, adjusted free cash flow in the implied range of 187.1 to 207.1, repurchases staying below free cash flow, and early refinancing of the 2028 notes.

Downside chain with observable triggers. Initiating condition: a freight, materials or tariff cost shock that pricing does not offset. First operational break: gross margin falling below the 29.9% of nine months 2026. Financial transmission: lower Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow while the dividend of 0.12 a share per quarter and the repurchase program continue. Leverage consequence: with net debt unchanged at 4,772.5, a fall of about 5% in trailing Adjusted EBITDA takes net leverage to 3.5x (Calculations), the level the stockholders agreement summary uses as a test. Liquidity and refinancing consequence: revolver drawings above the assumed nil balance would reduce liquidity below 1,063.8, and lenders would face the 3.875% notes due October 31, 2028 and the April 2029 notes with weaker cover. Triggers to watch: quarterly gross margin, add-backs, the revolver balance, repurchase pace against free cash flow, the sponsor's disclosed holding, and the covenant certificate when obtainable.
